sentences.text: Concavenator was a medium-sized primitive carnosaurian dinosaur measuring approximately 6 meters in length and weighing between 320 and 400 kilograms.

Unlike most relatives, this animal possessed tall neural spines on its last dorsal vertebrae that formed a sail-like structure, while two extremely high vertebrae in front of the hips formed a high, narrow, and pointed crest.
The skull measured 63 centimeters in length, and the skeleton features a series of small bumps on the ulnas and a small crest over the pelvis.
The fossil specimen preserved integument traces, including scale impressions on the feet and tail.
Concavenator possessed structures on its ulna resembling quill knobs, a feature previously known only in birds and feathered theropods.
The fossils were found by paleontologists José Luis Sanz, Francisco Ortega, and Fernando Escaso, who later named the genus Concavenator in 2010.
The holotype specimen, catalogued as MCCM-LH 6666, was described in 2010 by these researchers in the journal Nature.
Fossil evidence shows Concavenator had broad rectangular scales on its tail underside, bird-like scutes on its feet, and plantar pads on the soles of its feet.
Phylogenetic analyses recovered Concavenator as an early-diverging member of the Carcharodontosauridae family, which is the parent group of the genus.
The type species of the genus Concavenator is Concavenator corcovatus, and the animal is classified within the class Reptilia.
Concavenator corcovatus lived during the Early Cretaceous, specifically the Barremian stage, approximately 130 to 125 million years ago, and also between 125.77 and 121.4 million years ago.
The function of Concavenator's back crest is unknown, with hypotheses ranging from visual display to thermal regulation.
